Setting y=log t reduces the growth proof to z_next=2z+log(1+2/t²). Both parity subsequences of s/t remain bounded by the convergent product obtained from (s/t)_m (s/t)_{m+1}=1+2/t_m². This proves log N-log t=O(1), the exact limiting series, and its 8/(21·2^r·t_r²) tail bound. An independent last-occurrence dynamic program, matrix multiplication, and direct short-word set enumeration all agree; the standard-library verifier reports VERIFY_OK exhaustive_seeds=126 Thue_Morse_prefix_length=4096. Finite checks are corroboration, not the proof.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the two-integer exact recurrence for distinct scattered-subsequence support under complement doubling of every nonempty binary seed, plus an effective growth constant. The most relevant inspected primary paper (Lejeune–Leroy–Rigo, arXiv:1812.07330) proves k-binomial complexity results for factors of the Thue–Morse infinite word and studies multiplicities of selected scattered subwords, but does not state or entail the two-trace whole-block support recurrence. Berstel–Crochemore–Pin address embedding coefficients/congruences; Shallit–Shur–Zorcic address power-free complementary morphisms. The published-finding corpus matches concern different statistics and do not imply this recurrence. Residual risk of an implicit earlier matrix-product specialization is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The canonical Thue–Morse complement-doubling substitution is a central finite-word family; total distinct scattered-subsequence support is a different and natural invariant from embedding multiplicity, k-binomial equivalence classes and ordinary factor complexity. The result compresses exponentially large support sets to a fixed two-integer evolution for every seed, yields a nontrivial exact rapidly converging rate with quantitative error bound, and detects the precise exponential growth constant for the canonical infinite-word prefixes. The seed-uniform structural compression and infinite asymptotic theorem are the mathematical value; short sequence counts alone would not suffice.
